# Example output — SYNTHETIC, generated by `pp-watchdog selftest`

These files were produced against the six local fixture sites, not against any real
service, and they contain no real person's data. They exist so you can see the shape of
the output before running anything, and so the pipeline stays verifiable offline
(a sandbox or a plane with no Instagram route).

| file | what it is |
|---|---|
| `EXAMPLE-report-synthetic.md` | a full scan report: verdict table, takedown targets, coverage warning, manual searches |
| `EXAMPLE-notices-index.md` | the notice pack index, with the filing order that gets results |
| `EXAMPLE-notice-india-route.txt` | an IT Act §79(2)(b) / IT Rules 2021 Rule 3(2)(b) notice with machine evidence embedded |
| `EXAMPLE-notice-dmca.txt` | the §512(c)(3) variant for US-hosted infrastructure |

Regenerate at any time:

```bash
cd pp-watchdog && ./run.sh selftest
ls out/demo/work out/demo/work/notices
```

The fixture scenario: one mirror serving your current picture, one an old one, one a
larger file than Instagram displays, one blocking crawlers, one with nothing cached, and
one mirroring your bio text only — which is what the six verdict classes look like in the
wild, in one run.
